what: Third British national has suspected hantavirus infection, UK government says

clean_source_blocks.text: A third British national has suspected hantavirus in connection with an outbreak on board the cruise ship MV Hondius, the government has said. The patient is currently on the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha, where the ship stopped in mid-April. Two other British men have confirmed cases - one remains in a stable condition in the Netherlands after being evacuated from the ship on Wednesday, while the other remains in intensive care after being flown to South Africa last month. Five cases of hantavirus have been confirmed, including one of the three passengers on the cruise who died.
The patient is on the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha, which was visited by the cruise ship in April.

The MV Hondius is expected to dock in the Canary Islands at the weekend, where the government has confirmed it will be met by a chartered plane to fly the remaining British passengers and crew on the cruise ship back to the UK. Although none of the remaining Britons are currently displaying symptoms, they will be asked to isolate upon their return home. British national Martin Anstee, a 56-year-old retired police officer and an expedition guide on board the MV Hondius, was evacuated to the Netherlands on Wednesday alongside a 41-year-old Dutch crew member and a 65-year-old German. He remains in a stable condition and told the BBC that he was "fine". Another British passenger, 69, has a confirmed case and was medically evacuated to South Africa at the end of April.

PRAIA, Cape Verde — Two patients with hantavirus and one suspected of infection were evacuated Wednesday from a cruise ship at the center of a deadly outbreak, the U.N. health agency said. The ship then departed Cape Verde with nearly 150 people on board — isolated in their cabins — and headed to Spain's Canary Islands. Associated Press footage showed health workers in protective gear evacuating three patients. Two arrived at Amsterdam's airport Wednesday evening and were taken to separate hospitals. Three people have died, and one body remained on the ship, the World Health Organization said. Of eight recorded cases, five were confirmed by laboratory testing. Hantavirus usually spreads by inhaling contaminated rodent droppings and can spread person-to-person, though that is rare, according to the WHO, whose top epidemic expert said the risk to the public is low.

[Lähde: TIME]
An outbreak of the rare but highly deadly hantavirus on a cruise ship is causing international alarm, as authorities scramble to trace those who may have been exposed in a bid to curb its spread.

The World Health Organization says that to date, there are eight cases of hantavirus infection linked to the MV Hondius, which is currently en route to the Canary Islands. Three passengers who boarded the Hondius have died, one of whom was among five confirmed infected.

Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s director-general, has said that the overall public health risk from hantavirus remains low, and officials have dismissed the concern of hantavirus becoming a global pandemic threat like COVID-19.

But investigations continue as the situation grows complex. Nearly 150 passengers and crew members from 23 different nationalities are still on board the ship, while several other passengers disembarked before news of the outbreak emerged. Health authorities also confirmed that the hantavirus involved in the outbreak is the Andes strain, the only known strain transmissible between people and has been linked to infections with higher mortality.

Here are some of the countries linked to the recent hantavirus outbreak.

The MV Hondius departed Ushuaia, a city in southern Argentina, on April 1. One person on board the ship was an Argentine national.

Hantavirus is endemic in Argentina, but infections in the country are on the rise. The Argentine health ministry on Tuesday reported 101 hantavirus infections since June 2025, which is roughly double the caseload recorded over the same period the previous year, per the Associated Press.

While the source of the outbreak hasn’t been determined, the Argentine government has looked into whether the infections stemmed from the country. The AP reported, citing two unidentified investigators, that two of the three deaths, involving a married Dutch couple, may have ties to Ushuaia, with officials speculating that the couple contracted the virus during a bird-watching outing in the city that brought them to a landfill where they could have been exposed.

In a press briefing on Thursday, WHO director-general Ghebreyesus said that passengers from 12 countries—including Canada—had disembarked the MV Hondius at a stop on St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic. The cruise ship’s operator, Oceanwide Expeditions, also said Thursday that 30 individuals from at least 12 different nationalities disembarked on April 24.

payload.title: Kolmannella brittimatkustajalla epäillään hantavirustartuntaa risteilyaluksen tautiryppäässä
payload.summary: Britannian hallituksen mukaan kolmannella Britannian kansalaisella epäillään hantavirustartuntaa MV Hondius -risteilyalukseen liittyvässä tautiryppäässä. Aluksella on todettu viisi laboratoriovarmistettua tapausta, ja kolme ihmistä on kuollut.
payload.content:
Britannian hallituksen mukaan kolmannella Britannian kansalaisella epäillään hantavirustartuntaa MV Hondius -risteilyalukseen liittyvässä tautiryppäässä. Potilas on tällä hetkellä syrjäisellä Tristan da Cunhan saarella Atlantilla, missä alus pysähtyi huhtikuun puolivälissä. Tautiryppäässä on vahvistettu viisi hantavirustapausta, ja yksi tartunnan saaneista oli kolmen kuolleen risteilymatkustajan joukossa.

## Potilaita on evakuoitu hoitoon

Kahdella muulla brittiläisellä miehellä on vahvistettu hantavirustartunta. Toinen heistä on vakaassa tilassa Alankomaissa sen jälkeen, kun hänet evakuoitiin alukselta keskiviikkona. Toinen, 69-vuotias brittimatkustaja, on tehohoidossa Etelä-Afrikassa. Hänet lennätettiin hoitoon huhtikuun lopussa.

Alankomaihin evakuoitu britti on 56-vuotias Martin Anstee, eläkkeellä oleva poliisi ja MV Hondiuksella työskennellyt retkiopas. Hänet siirrettiin hoitoon yhdessä 41-vuotiaan hollantilaisen miehistön jäsenen ja 65-vuotiaan saksalaisen kanssa. Ansteen kerrotaan olevan vakaassa tilassa.

Maailman terveysjärjestön mukaan alukselta evakuoitiin keskiviikkona kaksi hantaviruspotilasta ja yksi tartuntaepäily. Associated Pressin kuvissa terveydenhuollon työntekijät suojavarusteissa siirsivät kolme potilasta pois alukselta. Kaksi heistä saapui Amsterdamin lentokentälle keskiviikkoiltana ja vietiin eri sairaaloihin.

## Alus matkalla Kanariansaarille

MV Hondius lähti Kap Verdestä kohti Espanjan Kanariansaaria lähes 150 ihmistä kyydissään. Aluksella olevien kerrottiin pysyneen eristettyinä hytteihinsä. WHO:n mukaan kolme ihmistä on kuollut, ja yksi ruumis oli yhä aluksella. Kahdeksasta kirjatusta tapauksesta viisi oli vahvistettu laboratoriotesteillä.

Aluksen odotetaan saapuvan Kanariansaarille viikonloppuna. Britannian hallituksen mukaan paikalle järjestetään tilauslento, jolla aluksella yhä olevat brittiläiset matkustajat ja miehistön jäsenet lennätetään takaisin Britanniaan.

Viranomaisten mukaan jäljellä olevilla briteillä ei tällä hetkellä ole oireita. Heitä kuitenkin pyydetään eristäytymään kotiinpaluun jälkeen varotoimena.

## WHO pitää yleisöriskiä pienenä

Hantavirus tarttuu yleensä hengitysteitse esimerkiksi jyrsijöiden eritteiden saastuttamasta pölystä. Maailman terveysjärjestön mukaan tartunta ihmisestä toiseen on mahdollinen mutta harvinainen. Järjestön epidemia-asiantuntijan arvion mukaan yleisölle aiheutuva riski on pieni.

Viisi tapausta on vahvistettu laboratoriotesteillä, ja kolme ihmistä on kuollut.
Aluksella olevat brittiläiset matkustajat ja miehistön jäsenet on määrä lennättää kotiin Kanariansaarilta.

article.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa annettuihin tietoihin Britannian hallituksen ja WHO:n ilmoituksista. Luokaksi valittu Ulkomaat, koska tapahtumat liittyvät kansainväliseen risteilyalukseen, Britannian kansalaisiin ja Atlantin alueeseen.
article.source_text:
A third British national has suspected hantavirus in connection with an outbreak on board the cruise ship MV Hondius, the government has said. The patient is currently on the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha, where the ship stopped in mid-April. Two other British men have confirmed cases - one remains in a stable condition in the Netherlands after being evacuated from the ship on Wednesday, while the other remains in intensive care after being flown to South Africa last month. Five cases of hantavirus have been confirmed, including one of the three passengers on the cruise who died.

The patient is on the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha, which was visited by the cruise ship in April.

The MV Hondius is expected to dock in the Canary Islands at the weekend, where the government has confirmed it will be met by a chartered plane to fly the remaining British passengers and crew on the cruise ship back to the UK. Although none of the remaining Britons are currently displaying symptoms, they will be asked to isolate upon their return home. British national Martin Anstee, a 56-year-old retired police officer and an expedition guide on board the MV Hondius, was evacuated to the Netherlands on Wednesday alongside a 41-year-old Dutch crew member and a 65-year-old German. He remains in a stable condition and told the BBC that he was "fine". Another British passenger, 69, has a confirmed case and was medically evacuated to South Africa at the end of April.

PRAIA, Cape Verde — Two patients with hantavirus and one suspected of infection were evacuated Wednesday from a cruise ship at the center of a deadly outbreak, the U.N. health agency said. The ship then departed Cape Verde with nearly 150 people on board — isolated in their cabins — and headed to Spain's Canary Islands. Associated Press footage showed health workers in protective gear evacuating three patients. Two arrived at Amsterdam's airport Wednesday evening and were taken to separate hospitals. Three people have died, and one body remained on the ship, the World Health Organization said. Of eight recorded cases, five were confirmed by laboratory testing. Hantavirus usually spreads by inhaling contaminated rodent droppings and can spread person-to-person, though that is rare, according to the WHO, whose top epidemic expert said the risk to the public is low.
